Apropos IMO is one of Linux most useful, but not too well known commands and something that you will likely not learn until after a fair amount of usage. This is unfortunate, as the command allows you to quickly search for commands by their man page descriptors. For instance if you have forgotten the name of a command, you can easily search for keywords that likely exist in it's man page description.... Example...

user@userPC:/$ apropos -a list content
dir (1) - list directory contents
git-ls-tree (1) - List the contents of a tree object
ls (1) - list directory contents
lsinitramfs (8) - list content of an initramfs image
ntfsls (8) - list directory contents on an NTFS filesystem
vdir (1) - list directory contents

Here is the typical format that I utilize when using apropos (utilizing the -a option to search for multiple keywords)

apropos -a search_term another_keyword "consecutive keywords in description"

Note that the use of quotes is only necessary when searching for an exact phrase.

I believe this is by far one of the most useful linux commands available and is too often not taught to users early on.
